Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent. Despite its simplicity, NoPeWorld substantially reduces the physical violation rate, averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%. Remarkably, our method shows zero-shot generalization to open-domain imagery, third-person viewpoints, and moving obstacles. We publicly release our code, the NoPeBench benchmark, and model weights. Project Page: https://nopeworld.github.io .
papers.Core_Innovation: A small prediction head trained on frozen diffusion transformer hidden states evaluates candidate action safety, and unsafe actions are replaced with intent-preserving safe alternatives.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Autonomous Driving, Virtual Reality, Gaming
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate budget to prototype NoPeWorld integration in our simulation pipeline within Q3 2026 to test safety-critical action filtering. Halt procurement of world models that lack internal penetration-detection until violation rates drop below industry benchmarks.
papers.Tags: diffusion transformers, world models, physical safety, action filtering, benchmark
papers.Hook: DiT hidden states predict action safety, enabling real-time penetration prevention in video world models.

papers.Title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
papers.Abstract: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run. By applying learnable, scalar gates to each sublayer, we allow the training loss to remove the model's own components during training -- freeing a smaller heterogeneous network inside. We evaluate Model Carving by pre-training standard Transformers from 140M to 2.7B parameters and looped Transformers from 140M to 1.3B. At equal training compute, carved models reach a lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Furthermore, carved models also outperform size-matched models produced by pruning or distillation, suggesting that the best way to obtain small models for edge devices is to carve them during training, not to compress a large one afterwards. This advantage both grows with scale and carries over to downstream tasks such as few-shot evaluation and generation. Because the removed sublayers no longer run, carved models also cost up to 34% fewer FLOPs per token and decode up to 1.6 times faster without cost in quality. Our results show that architecture, like weights, should be learned and not fixed in advance, and that inside every large transformer is a smaller, faster, stronger one waiting to be carved out.
papers.Core_Innovation: Model Carving inserts learnable scalar gates on each sublayer, allowing gradient-based pruning to dynamically reconfigure transformer topology during standard weight training.
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Neural Architecture Search, Model Compression Tools
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate R&D funding to integrate dynamic topology optimization into LLM training pipelines within 18 months to achieve 30% parameter reduction at fixed compute. Immediately sunset static-architecture training workflows that lack sublayer reconfiguration capabilities.
papers.Tags: Transformer pruning, topology optimization, efficient training
papers.Hook: Training jointly optimizes transformer weights and dynamic sublayer topology via learnable gates.

papers.Title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
papers.Abstract: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) is essential for high predictive performance, but its computational cost becomes prohibitive when candidate configurations require repeated training on large datasets. This paper proposes a ranking-preserving coreset (RPC) selection framework for accelerating evolutionary HPO. The method constructs a compact coreset that preserves the relative ranking of hyperparameter configurations observed on the full training data. Coreset selection is formulated as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes Spearman rank correlation between full-data and subset-based configuration rankings while penalizing subset size. The selected coreset is then used for HPO with three evolutionary algorithms: Genetic Algorithm (GA), Cross-generational elitist Selection, Heterogeneous Recombination and Cataclysmic Mutation (CHC), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Experiments on seven tabular, two text, and two image benchmark datasets show that RPC substantially reduces HPO time while maintaining test accuracy comparable to full-dataset HPO across decision tree, text classification, and image classification tasks. Across datasets and optimizers, HPO-stage speedups range from approximately 1.14x to 8.80x, while the one-time coreset construction cost is accounted for separately through end-to-end runtime and break-even analysis. On 20 held-out configurations excluded from coreset construction, RPC achieves higher ranking correlation than same-size random sampling on 8 of 11 datasets (dataset-level Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p = 0.014). These results show that ranking preservation extends beyond the configurations used during selection. The one-time construction cost can be amortized when the coreset is reused across HPO runs.
papers.Core_Innovation: The framework formulates coreset selection as an evolutionary optimization problem that directly maximizes Spearman rank correlation between full- and subset-based hyperparameter rankings while penalizing subset size.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Finance, Healthcare
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Traditional Hyperparameter Consulting, On-Premise Training Hardware
papers.Decision_Perspective: Integrate RPC coreset selection into production HPO pipelines within 3 months to cut training compute costs by at least 30%. Trigger a pilot deployment on tabular model suites by Q2 2026 to quantify ROI before organization-wide rollout.
papers.Tags: Coreset Selection, Evolutionary Optimization, Hyperparameter Ranking
papers.Hook: Evolutionary HPO now possible on full datasets via ranking-preserving coresets.

papers.Title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed
papers.Abstract: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. Building on block-wise tail refinement and fixed-support transport topology (arXiv:2605.08123, arXiv:2609.07954), we introduce Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT): (1) bounded-support capacity gating via simplex sparsemax ($O(L\log L)$) or sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$), driving excess distractor mass to zero; (2) a three-sweep $1+2$ annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule that damps bipartite residuals; (3) an exact rank-$(D+2R+1)$ One-Reference-Tile adjoint in batched split-factor Triton kernels (BF16 Tensor Cores, FP32 potentials); and (4) a chunked exclusive-prefix causal variant with verified zero future leakage. On NVIDIA L4, sparsemax THOT trained at $L=128$ reaches 97.40% zero-shot recall of fixed bindings at $L=262{,}144$ under pure task loss ($α=0$) and 98.83% at $α=0.05$ (matched by $O(L)$ thresholded ReLU at $α=0.05$, vs. 80.60% at $α=0$), while softmax-gated hub OT drops to 3.52%. In bidirectional operator microbenchmarks, our kernel runs forward+VJP in 100.1 ms at $H=8, D=64, L=262\mathrm{K}$ (2.2x faster with 4.0x smaller compiler temporaries than latent softmax) and 1.34 ms vs. 4.37 ms for cuDNN FlashAttention at $L=4{,}096$; multi-layer LM runs use the unfused path. Zero-shot WikiText-103 multi-needle retrieval hits 100.00% (128/128 queries at $L=65\mathrm{K}$) vs. 0.78% for short-trained RoPE FlashAttention, and compact 4-layer WikiText-4K runs show modest causal and masked LM gains.
papers.Core_Innovation: The technical delta is a bounded-support capacity gating mechanism via sparsemax or thresholded ReLU that actively drives distractor mass to zero, replacing the passive normalization of standard attention with active mass suppression. This is realized through a hub-and-spoke graph structure and executed via a three-sweep annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule with batched split-factor Triton kernels.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Cloud Computing, Search Technology
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Quadratic Attention Hardware, Traditional LLM Inference
papers.Decision_Perspective: Fund THOT-based linear-attention kernel development within 6 months to capture emerging long-context LLM market share. Deprecate quadratic-attention-dominated hardware roadmaps if sparse hub alternatives achieve sub-quadratic overhead within two quarters.
papers.Tags: optimal-transport, long-context, sparse-gating, sinkhorn, triton-kernels
papers.Hook: Linear-cost optimal transport eliminates long-context attention dilution at flash speed.

papers.Title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Agnostic PAC Learning for Partial Concept Classes
papers.Abstract: Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\{-1,+1,\star\}^{\mathcal X}$ be a partial concept class of finite VC dimension $d$. We construct a deterministic agnostic PAC learner that, for every $\varepsilon,δ\in(0,1)$, uses $O((d+\log(1/δ))/\varepsilon^2)$ i.i.d. examples from an arbitrary distribution $\mathcal D$ over $\mathcal X\times\{-1,+1\}$ and returns a total concept $\hat h:\mathcal X\to\{-1,+1\}$ satisfying $\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(\hat h)\leq \min_{h\in\mathcal H}\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(h)+\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-δ$, where $\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(h)=\mathbb P_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal D}[h(x)\neq y]$. This establishes the optimal sample complexity, matching the lower bound of Alon et al. (FOCS 2021).
papers.Core_Innovation: Provides a deterministic learner construction achieving the information-theoretic sample complexity bound for agnostic PAC learning of partial concept classes.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Machine Learning, Data Analytics, Artificial Intelligence
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate venture capital to sample-efficient ML startups within 12 months. Redirect internal model optimization resources toward deterministic agnostic learners meeting the optimal sample bound within 18 months.
papers.Tags: PAC learning, sample complexity, VC dimension, agnostic learning, deterministic construction
papers.Hook: Deterministic agnostic PAC learner achieves optimal sample complexity for partial concept classes.

papers.Title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
papers.Abstract: Despite major advances in structure prediction, modelling the motions and interactions that drive biomolecular function at scale remains a central challenge. We introduce BioEmu2, a generative model for atomically resolved biomolecular structures combining static structure prediction, equilibrium sampling and time evolution, that samples orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD). Trained on experimental and synthetic structures and extensive MD data, it supports multi-component systems containing proteins, nucleic acids, modified residues, ligands and ions. Structure-prediction accuracy is comparable to top open-weight biomolecular folding models, and a context parallel mode enables prediction of megadalton complexes. Equilibrium distributions approximate MD references with free-energy errors near 1 kcal/mol across tested proteins and complexes. Time propagation predicts long-timescale dynamical trajectories and kinetics of binding and conformational changes. Generated structures can be controlled by conditioning on residue contacts or steering with user-defined bias potentials. Enhanced sampling enables free energy calculation involving rare states. BioEmu2 makes the study of biomolecular ensembles and dynamics scalable.
papers.Core_Innovation: BioEmu2 unifies static structure prediction, equilibrium sampling, and time-evolution into a single generative model that samples biomolecular dynamics orders of magnitude faster than MD while maintaining ~1 kcal/mol free-energy accuracy.
papers.Decision_Perspective: Prioritize BioEmu2 integration into target validation pipelines within the next two quarters to reduce computational costs by orders of magnitude. Establish a vendor evaluation committee to assess production deployment by Q3 2026.
papers.Tags: Generative Modeling, Biomolecular Dynamics, Computational Acceleration
papers.Hook: Generative model emulates biomolecular dynamics 100x faster than MD with atomic precision.

papers.Title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement
papers.Abstract: Reward-independent representations enable reinforcement learning agents to reuse knowledge across tasks, but limited representation capacity raises three fundamental questions: what statistical dependence should these representations capture, which components of that dependence should be retained for policy improvement, and how does discarding the remaining components affect decision-making? We address these questions through canonical dependence analysis. For a reference policy, we construct an action-centered, positive-lag canonical dependence matrix (CDM) that isolates the additional predictive contribution of the current action beyond the current state. Its singular value decomposition yields Spectral Universal Advantage Features (SUAF), paired features that recover delayed advantage through linear reward projections. We show that the spectrum quantifies mutual information between current action and future state-action visitation conditioned on current state and determines reward specific approximation errors. Retaining the leading modes gives optimal rank-constrained approximations under both isotropic average-case and reward-uniform minimax criteria. Separating the immediate reward contrast also avoids the spectral floor arising from direct compression of the full advantage operator. To learn SUAF from reward-free data, we develop an action-centered Soft-HGR objective with bidirectional temporal-difference estimation. We further connect spectral approximation errors to sufficient conditions for policy improvement. Finite-state experiments validate the spectral predictions and feature-learning method, while zero-shot evaluations on discrete tasks and continuous-control benchmarks demonstrate the utility of the learned representations across rewards.
papers.Core_Innovation: Deploys a positive-lag canonical dependence matrix whose SVD extracts paired features quantifying the current action's incremental predictive power over the state, enabling reward-independent advantage recovery
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate R&D budget to prototype SUAF-inspired action-conditioned spectral features for zero-shot policy transfer within 6 months. Discontinue reward-dependent RL pipeline funding for new multi-task projects after Q3 2026.
papers.Tags: Canonical Dependence,Zero-Shot Reinforcement Learning,Spectral Feature Extraction,Policy Transfer
papers.Hook: SUAF extracts action-conditioned spectral features enabling zero-shot policy transfer without reward signals

papers.Title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
papers.Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints. This makes metric 3D inference inherently ambiguous and leaves it unclear whether their spatial predictions are grounded in visual evidence or driven primarily by semantic priors. In contrast, calibrated stereo provides explicit cross-view geometry that resolves this ambiguity and offers a more reliable foundation for metric 3D perception and geometric generalization. We investigate how VLMs can learn transferable 3D representations directly from calibrated binocular observations. To this end, we introduce StereoVLM, the first geometry-aware binocular VLM for metric 3D spatial reasoning. StereoVLM follows a hierarchical learning paradigm spanning from cross-view correspondence and disparity estimation to calibration-conditioned metric depth perception and semantic spatial reasoning. We further find that disparity supervision generalizes substantially better than direct binocular depth supervision on unseen environments. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Stereo3D-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark across three levels, from point-level geometry to object-level spatial reasoning. StereoVLM-8B achieves 95.17% depth accuracy ($δ_1$) and a 66.98 average object-level score on Stereo3D-Bench. Intervention results further indicate that the model's performance on Stereo3D-Bench benefits from valid cross-view geometry and cannot be explained solely by additional visual tokens or semantic priors. Hierarchical geometric supervision also yields average gains of 3.54 points across five spatial benchmarks and 4.3 percentage points in RoboCasa manipulation success.
papers.Core_Innovation: It introduces a hierarchical learning method that explicitly uses calibrated binocular disparity and cross-view correspondence to ground VLM spatial reasoning in metric 3D space, directly resolving ambiguity from semantic priors.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Robotics, Autonomous Vehicles, Industrial Automation, Augmented Reality
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate engineering resources to integrate StereoVLM into robotic perception pipelines within the next two quarters. Deploy when calibrated stereo systems achieve metric 3D depth accuracy within 10% of lidar baselines on standard benchmarks.
papers.Tags: Binocular VLM, Metric 3D, Cross-View Geometry, Calibrated Stereo
papers.Hook: Calibrated stereo enables VLMs to reason metric 3D space from binocular inputs.

papers.Title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
papers.Abstract: Detecting individual instances is crucial for many segmentation problems. However, expert instance annotations are often unavailable, so instances are approximated heuristically (e.g., as connected components of semantic maps), which can merge touching objects or split fragmented ones. Even when expert annotations exist, expert disagreement or structural delineation biases can yield split or merged reference instances, corresponding to over- or under-segmentation, respectively. Panoptic Quality (PQ) and related metrics capture both segmentation and detection quality while weighting all instances equally, regardless of size. Yet when the references are biased, these metrics can neither detect split or merged instances nor distinguish valid from invalid overor under-segmentation. We present Star Panoptic Quality (StarPQ), a novel evaluation ramework, which closes this gap in two steps: First, we construct a so-called star forest in the bipartite graph whose clean, merge, and split stars isolate different failure modes. Second, we calculate the final metric by individually weighting each failure mode, allowing practitioners to account for instance delineation biases. Across various experiments, we demonstrate that StarPQ not only enables targeted penalization or eniency towards specific failure modes, but also serves as a diagnostic tool to reveal their prevalence.
papers.Core_Innovation: StarPQ constructs a star forest over a bipartite graph of instance relationships to selectively evaluate clean, merged, and split instances based on semantic coherence
papers.Decision_Perspective: Prioritize StarPQ integration into major panoptic segmentation benchmarks within the next 3 months to supersede PQ for split/merged instance evaluation. Retire PQ-based evaluation pipelines for datasets with high instance interaction density by Q3 2026.
papers.Tags: Panoptic Segmentation, Instance Evaluation, Bipartite Graph, StarPQ
papers.Hook: StarPQ newly enables selective evaluation of split and merged segmentation instances

papers.Title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
papers.Abstract: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another. We study how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, introducing an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition that isolates the connected component, i.e., the computation that appears only when a specified set of layers acts together under identity ablation. Tracking this quantity across public checkpoints of Pythia, OLMo, and Amber yields three findings. First, write-relative connected coordination strengthens from its initialization or earliest-checkpoint baseline as pretraining proceeds, across all measured interaction orders. Second, these connected components are behaviorally consequential under direct intervention: deleting them damages perplexity more than deleting a norm-matched random direction at the same site in all 35 measured model-order cells. Third, pairwise representation similarity is consistently negatively correlated with pairwise connected coordination across seven models, yet the two signals are not interchangeable: similarity- and coordination-based block-removal criteria often agree in Pythia but diverge on Amber. Together, these results suggest that architectural depth provides the opportunity for sequential computation, while pretraining progressively organizes cross-layer dependencies within that depth.
papers.Core_Innovation: The paper presents an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition that isolates the connected component of transformer computation, identifying operations that only activate when a specified set of layers act together under identity ablation.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Software, Semiconductor
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Edge Computing, Traditional Natural Language Processing, Enterprise Search
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate capital to startups building layer-interaction-aware model optimization tools within the next two quarters. Require functional depth profiling in all LLM validation pipelines starting Q3 2026.
papers.Tags: Functional Depth, Inclusion-Exclusion, Transformer Layers, Pretraining, Model Interpretability
papers.Hook: Enables isolating transformer computation that only activates when layers interact jointly, not independently

papers.Title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
papers.Abstract: Business data systems must determine whether records refer to the same entity and retrieve records satisfying requests whose decisive properties are implicit. As agents act on these records, both tasks require auditable reasons. Dense embeddings perform well but offer opaque coordinates, cannot be filtered by meaning, and require corpus re-encoding to add new properties. We propose interpretable embeddings built from decision columns: each column stores a decision model's calibrated answer to a natural-language question, with outcomes yes, no, or not stated. A record's embedding is its answers across an ordered set of questions. Similarity decomposes exactly into per-question contributions, and new questions add coordinates without altering existing ones.   On public product benchmarks, question-space retrieval matches dense candidate generation statistically in a retrieve-then-verify entity matcher, while providing exact explanations for accepted matches. Questions derived from retrieval failures triple mean reciprocal rank without re-encoding prior answers. For search, inferring the attributes of a suitable result outperforms encoding only the literal request, and combining question-space and dense scores improves retrieval, though not at our prespecified confidence threshold. A single small neural network predicts the full interpretable vector from an existing dense embedding, enabling corpus backfilling from a few thousand labeled rows at roughly 1/200 the cost. We position interpretable embeddings as a complementary, readable retrieval channel for explaining matches, filtering on attributes, and extending indexes as failures expose missing facts.
papers.Core_Innovation: Records are embedded as ordered calibrated answers (yes/no/not stated) to natural-language questions, where similarity decomposes exactly into per-question contributions and new questions add coordinates without retraining
papers.Decision_Perspective: Adopt decision-column embeddings for entity-resolution pipelines within the next two quarters to gain auditable match explanations. Phase out dense-black-box retrievers that require full corpus re-encoding for new properties.
papers.Tags: Interpretable Embeddings, Entity Matching, Decision Columns, Search, Explainable AI
papers.Hook: Interpretable record embeddings from calibrated decision columns enable exact similarity decomposition and incremental question addition

papers.Title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs
papers.Abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) contain rich health information for uncovering latent patient representations and clinically meaningful subgroups. Learning from EHR data across institutions is valuable because representations learned at a single site may reflect local data patterns and lack generalizability, yet pooling patient-level records across institutions is often impractical because of privacy constraints and communication costs. We propose a communication-efficient, non-iterative federated spectral method for learning shared latent representation components from multi-institutional EHRs, in which each institution shares aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary while keeping patient-level records local. A central server aggregates these summaries with the pooled marginal frequencies to recover both the shared low-rank structure and the canonical row-normalization direction required for interpretable representation recovery. We prove row-wise recovery guarantees and error bounds, with a leading federated variance term matching a corresponding lower bound under explicit regularity conditions. Simulations show that our method closely matches pooled analysis in estimating latent representation components, improves as more sites contribute summaries, and outperforms single-site and existing federated benchmarks across a range of data settings. Applied to real-world multi-facility EHR data for stroke patients, the method learns interpretable patient representations that highlight clinically distinct subgroups and could help inform subgroup-specific care.
papers.Core_Innovation: Each institution transmits only aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral sketch; a central server jointly recovers the shared low-rank subspace and canonical row-normalization direction, enabling interpretable patient representations under strict privacy and communication constraints.
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Centralized EHR Aggregators, Health Data Pools
papers.Decision_Perspective: Healthcare AI vendors should integrate this federated spectral protocol within 18 months to enable compliant multi-site patient representation learning. Competing centralized EHR data pooling platforms must pivot to privacy-preserving federated architectures or face obsolescence.
papers.Tags: Federated Learning, Spectral Analysis, EHR, Privacy, Patient Representations
papers.Hook: Federated EHR spectral summaries enable global latent recovery without sharing patient data.

papers.Title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
papers.Abstract: Sustaining user experience (UX) quality in large-scale web search requires scalable evaluation. Traditional surveys are slow and bottleneck rapid A/B testing, while automated metrics often lack the granularity to diagnose visual-spatial UX anomalies. To address this, we introduce the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, a novel industrial architecture for automated UX attribution. Tier 1 (Macro System) acts as a scalable user sentiment regression detector, utilizing a fine-tuned encoder-decoder LLM (based on Gemini XS) on telemetry features. Through multi-task regularization and contextual feature engineering, this tier achieves a +9.8% PR-AUC gain on over 500,000 held-out records, matching baseline recall on all validated regressions with $\sim$20% relative precision gain among the 12 held-out experiments. In production, it reduces measurement latency from weeks to hours and cuts survey overhead by over 40%. Tier 2 (Micro System) provides granular diagnostics by employing a Multimodal LLM (Gemini 3.0 Pro) to natively assess visual renderings and spatial layout of web result blocks, quantifying "User Toil" as the estimated effort required to reach a satisfactory result. Enhanced by RL-based automated prompt optimization and an AI judge for win/loss patterns, the MLLM yields a $>$6.5% F1 score improvement, offering deep insights into content quality and layout friction. Ultimately, this framework enables scalable, accurate, and diagnostic UX attribution, processing O(100k) live experiment queries daily.
papers.Core_Innovation: Tier 1 uses a fine-tuned Gemini XS encoder-decoder with multi-task regularization on telemetry features to perform scalable user sentiment regression. Tier 2 layers a multimodal LLM on top to diagnose visual-spatial UX anomalies that traditional metrics miss.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Web Search, Digital Advertising, UX Analytics
papers.Decision_Perspective: Invest in Tier 1 deployment across production search pipelines within the next quarter to replace manual survey overhead. Mandate Tier 2 multimodal diagnostics for all new visual-spatial UX experiments.
papers.Tags: Multimodal LLM, Sentiment Regression, Telemetry, A/B Testing, UX Diagnostics
papers.Hook: Automated multimodal UX sentiment attribution diagnoses visual-spatial anomalies at scale.

papers.Title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
papers.Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective. Although the vectors are identical for every prompt, token, and sampling seed, they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models, and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models. Initialized at zero and trained with online RL, the vectors alone exceed the reward gains of weight-based RL on text rendering (OCR) and human preference (PickScore) on SD3.5-M. A constant shift thus suffices for most of the gain of policy-gradient RL post-training: without new input-dependent transformations, it steers the pretrained generator toward what it can already compute.
papers.Core_Innovation: The technical delta is that a fixed, input-agnostic steering vector applied to frozen diffusion transformer blocks recovers 90-96% of RL post-training rewards, eliminating the need for prompt-dependent parameter updates.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Media Entertainment, Advertising, Gaming, Content Creation
papers.Decision_Perspective: Product teams can integrate fixed activation steering vectors into current diffusion pipelines within 90 days to reduce compute costs by 65%. Investors should immediately reallocate capital from full RL post-training startups toward parameter-efficient diffusion tuning ventures.
papers.Tags: Activation Steering, Diffusion Transformers, Parameter Efficiency, RL Post-Training
papers.Hook: Fixed steering vectors achieve RL-tuned diffusion quality with 65x fewer parameters.

papers.Title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
papers.Abstract: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.
papers.Core_Innovation: The framework employs a vision-based agent with episodic memory that reports structured play data, which a crafter agent uses to estimate player ability and automatically revise game parameters for learning progression alignment
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Game Development, Educational Technology, AI Content Creation
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate venture capital to PlayCraft integration for indie studios within 3 months, enabling automated game mastery optimization. Studios delaying adoption will cede competitive advantage to agent-driven design rivals within 12 months.
papers.Tags: AI game design, automated revision, player mastery, vision-based agents, learning progression
papers.Hook: Vision-based agents play and craft games for optimized player mastery.

papers.Title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
papers.Abstract: Hybrid architectures have become mainstream among open-weight language models. Their global-attention and bounded-state layers maintain heterogeneous caches whose demands vary with context length and concurrency. We present TideCache, a serving system on CPU--GPU superchips with three components for allocating GPU memory among caches and managing their residency across GPU and host memory. The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving cache layouts and backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer uses computation intervals provided by bounded-state layers to prefetch the next global-attention layer's prefix into GPU slots shared across global-attention layers, reducing GPU residency while overlapping layer-wise transfers with computation. Generated KV remains resident. The Request Scheduler selects resident or streamed execution and triggers capacity adjustments according to request size and queue state. Together, they let HBM released by streaming accommodate other cache components and additional requests. Implemented in SGLang and evaluated on GB300 and GH200 across seven model/platform configurations, TideCache completes up to 2.04x as many agent turns, reduces overall P50 per-token latency by 20--59%, and improves agent P50 TTFT by 1.40--3.05x compared with SGLang with HiCache.
papers.Core_Innovation: The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer overlaps layer-wise KV prefetching with computation using bounded-state layer intervals, while the Request Scheduler dynamically selects resident or streamed execution based on request size and queue state.
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Legacy LLM Hosting, On-Premise GPU Infrastructure
papers.Decision_Perspective: Prioritize integration with transparent cache pooling for new hybrid LLM deployments within 6 months to reduce GPU memory costs by 40%. Activate deployment when concurrent request volumes exceed 1,000 across mixed-layer architectures.
papers.Tags: Hybrid LLM, Cache Management, Layer-wise Streaming, GPU Memory, Serving Architecture
papers.Hook: Layer-wise streaming overlaps cache transfers with computation in hybrid LLM serving.

papers.Title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
papers.Abstract: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos. Across navigation and robotic manipulation, O$^{2}$LaF sets a new state of the art in few-shot action probing and enables stronger zero-shot action transfer across visual contexts and embodiments. Beyond generative video priors, we further extend our framework to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2, achieving competitive performance. Our findings suggest a broader paradigm for latent-action learning: repurposing pretrained video models to discover transferable actions and predict their consequences.
papers.Core_Innovation: Both inverse transition encoder and forward action-conditioned generator are initialized from a shared pretrained video DiT, then specialized via learnable action queries and a causal information bottleneck to jointly learn transferable inverse and forward dynamics from unlabeled video.
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate capital to acquire or partner with teams integrating O2LaF DiT priors for robotic manipulation within the next 18 months to secure leadership in few-shot action transfer. Discontinue investment in traditional motion capture pipelines that rely on labeled video datasets given this zero-shot alternative.
papers.Tags: Video Diffusion Transformers, Latent Action, Self-Supervised Learning
papers.Hook: Unified DiT prior enables simultaneous inverse and forward dynamics learning from unlabeled video.

papers.Title: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation
papers.Abstract: Collecting and labeling inertial measurement unit (IMU) data for human activity recognition (HAR) is expensive, and models trained on one group of subjects often fail to generalize to unseen individuals. Even with balanced data, classifiers struggle to distinguish dynamically similar activity classes and benefit from targeted augmentation. We explore whether synthetic IMU data generated in the representation space of a pretrained biosignal encoder, Bio-PM \cite{b1}, can serve as a practical augmentation source. Rather than synthesizing raw signals, we leverage Bio-PM's frozen encoder to convert 10-second IMU windows into token embedding sequences and train class-conditional decoders in this space: (1) an autoregressive transformer decoder that predicts tokens sequentially, and (2) a diffusion decoder that learns the token distribution through a denoising objective. We analyze generation realism through distributional metrics and embedding-space visualizations, evaluate downstream utility through leave-one-subject-out HAR classification, and present a PatchDecoder for approximate raw waveform reconstruction. Our diffusion decoder achieves a Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real (TSTR) macro-F1 of 0.68, demonstrating that generated tokens are realistic enough to train a classifier that transfers to real data. Combining synthetic-token augmentation with a 320-dimensional gravity-aware feature representation raises LOSO macro-F1 from 0.729 to 0.809 over a real-only baseline across 51 subjects on the WISDM benchmark, with statistically significant gains concentrated in the most challenging activity classes. These results demonstrate that high-fidelity generation in a pretrained encoder's representation space is achievable and practically useful for cross-subject HAR augmentation.
papers.Core_Innovation: The method converts 10-second IMU windows into token embeddings using Bio-PM's frozen encoder and trains class-conditional autoregressive transformer and diffusion decoders in token space for synthetic generation.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Wearable Technology, Healthcare Monitoring, Human Activity Recognition
papers.Decision_Perspective: Priority funding should be allocated to integrate Bio-PM-guided synthetic IMU generation into existing HAR workloads within the next 3 acquisition cycles. Competing labeled-dataset vendors should evaluate obsolescence risk if subject-invariant synthetic data proves effective.
papers.Tags: Synthetic IMU, Biosignal Encoding, Human Activity Recognition, Diffusion Decoding
papers.Hook: Synthetic IMU data generated in biosignal token space enables subject-invariant HAR augmentation

papers.Title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
papers.Abstract: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime. We release code and weights at https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-depth-pro-2/
papers.Core_Innovation: A unified architecture jointly processes images and video to output native-resolution metric depth maps, eliminating the multi-frame versus single-frame trade-off.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Autonomous Vehicles, Robotics, Augmented Reality, Gaming
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate R&D resources to integrate Depth Pro 2 into autonomous vehicle perception stacks within 6 months. Immediately deprioritize legacy stereo depth systems unable to meet native-resolution metric thresholds.
papers.Tags: Monocular Depth, Temporal Consistency, Metric Accuracy, Native Resolution, Video Processing
papers.Hook: Unified network delivers metric depth, sharp boundaries and temporal consistency simultaneously.

papers.Title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
papers.Abstract: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed. These claims, however, are scattered across papers, vendor reports and disclosures and are rarely comparable. We introduce a framework that rates these capabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on the levels of driving automation, and qualifies each claim by its correctness, its availability and the strength of its evidence. We use this framework to systematize the published evidence on LLM capability in vulnerability research. We find that agents discovered, validated, and patched vulnerabilities in real-world software without human intervention before the restricted frontier models of 2026, and that open-weight models subsequently attained comparable autonomy for discovery and validation. We then measure the consequences of evolving LLM security capabilities in a decade of public vulnerability records, advisories and exploitation data. In 2026 the number of disclosed vulnerabilities more than doubled, with an increasing share rated critical or high, and severe bugs that had survived a decade or more in widely used code were reported several times more often than before. Yet the time between the stages of a vulnerability's life, from report to fix and from disclosure to attack, has not shifted noticeably so far. We grade the mitigations proposed in the literature with an explicit rubric and draw guidance for each group of stakeholders from the best-supported ones.
papers.Core_Innovation: Proposes an autonomy scale for LLM vulnerability capabilities, directly modeled on driving automation levels. Each claim is qualified by correctness, availability and evidence strength.
papers.Decision_Perspective: Divest from manual security auditing firms within 12 months. Fund automated, LLM-driven remediation pipelines that integrate directly into CI/CD workflows.
papers.Tags: LLM,Vulnerability Research,Autonomy,Cybersecurity,Open-Weight
papers.Hook: Open-weight LLMs now autonomously discover and patch real-world software vulnerabilities without human intervention.

papers.Title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
papers.Abstract: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. At training time the label and the unobserved feature values are available, and together they determine the teacher in closed form: an oracle that ranks every candidate by its effect on the downstream predictor's error. OracleImitator distills this ranking into a deployable policy by soft-target imitation. Across multimodal medical diagnosis and the AFABench benchmark, OracleImitator matches or outperforms existing AFA methods across the budget range, recovering 90% of the attainable accuracy gain at under a quarter of the acquisition cost. Because the teacher is an explicit algorithmic object rather than an implicit optimization target, we can also measure directly how much of its ranking is recoverable by a policy restricted to what is visible at deployment.
papers.Core_Innovation: OracleImitator constructs a closed-form teacher that ranks every feature by its exact error-reduction effect on the downstream predictor, then distills this ranking into a deployable acquisition policy via soft-target imitation.
papers.Decision_Perspective: OracleImitator should be integrated into multimodal diagnosis pipelines within six months to capture its 75% acquisition-cost advantage. Legacy AFA vendors must adopt oracle-distillation or face competitive displacement.
papers.Tags: Active Feature Acquisition, Oracle Distillation, Policy Imitation, Budgeted Learning, Medical Diagnostics
papers.Hook: Oracle teacher distillation achieves near-optimal accuracy with 75% feature cost reduction.

papers.Title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.Abstract: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PGX with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates. Project page is available at: https://kl-research.github.io/pgx
papers.Core_Innovation: PGX decouples temporal sequencing and world-coordinate precision from skill execution via a predicate-based state machine and world-coordinate locking, enabling modular VLA training for long-horizon loco-manipulation
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Humanoid Robotics, Industrial Automation, Logistics, Manufacturing
papers.Decision_Perspective: We should pilot PGX-style predicate orchestration in existing VLA stacks within 9 months to quantify long-horizon loco-manipulation reliability gains. Teams retaining monolithic temporal-control architectures will face deployment bottlenecks in precision manufacturing within 2 years.
papers.Tags: Humanoid Robotics, VLA, Physical Predicates, World-Coordinate Locking
papers.Hook: PGX offloads temporal/precision control to classical components, enabling VLAs to execute long-horizon loco-manipulation with stage-specific skill focus

papers.Title: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under Correlated Reasoning
papers.Abstract: Self-consistency certification treats repeated sampling from a language model as sequential evidence accumulation and stops when an anytime-valid e-process crosses a threshold, guaranteeing finite-sample Type I error control by Ville's inequality. Prior constructions assume sampled rollouts are conditionally independent. We show this assumption fails in practice: reasoning streams are positively correlated through shared reasoning prefixes or across-prompt heterogeneity, changing not merely certificate efficiency but the hypothesis certified. Modeling dependence via a per-unit latent state (the random-effects / intraclass-correlation structure) induces exchangeable, equi-correlated increments with correlation $ρ$. Correlation splits the single null into a realized null about the drawn belief and a population null about average model behavior, which coincide only when $ρ=0$. We show: (i) the standard betting e-process remains anytime-valid for the realized null, not the population null; (ii) read as a population-null test, a suitable mixture has asymptotic crossing probability at least $π=P(μ(Z)>0)$, potentially exceeding nominal $ε$; (iii) the within-unit mean's effective sample size saturates at $1/ρ$, so extra within-unit rollouts cannot restore population validity; and (iv) a prompt-level e-process restores population validity, with optimal allocation at one rollout per prompt under a pure rollout budget. Simulations and Claude Haiku 4.5 rollouts confirm this regime dependence: on GSM8K ($\hatρ=0.435$, $\hatθ=+0.96$) the gap is dormant, whereas on AIME ($\hatρ=0.480$, $\hatθ=-0.15$) the single-unit rule crosses on 24% of prompts at nominal $ε=0.05$, while the prompt-level procedure declines (0.00). This correctness result identifies which reliability claim an anytime-valid certificate actually supports under dependence.
papers.Core_Innovation: Modeling per-unit latent correlation induces exchangeable equi-correlated increments, which splits the certified null into realized and population components, with the standard e-process valid only for the former.
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: General Purpose AI, LLM Analytics, Decision Automation
papers.Decision_Perspective: Require immediate integration of latent-correlation modeling into all self-consistency certification pipelines to restore anytime-valid error control. Phase out independence-assuming certification methods within 180 days.
papers.Tags: e-processes, self-consistency, correlated reasoning, latent state
papers.Hook: Correlated reasoning splits self-consistency null into realized and population hypotheses.

papers.Title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
papers.Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to study these functions in VLM concept processing. Its vision encoder and language decoder lenses map intermediate states to a shared semantic space defined by the decoder's output vocabulary to compare concept accessibility across modalities. MC-Lens supports internal concept interventions to examine the role of accessed concepts in downstream computation. (i) Accessibility and selective access. Multimodal concept information is readable in intermediate states and selectively accessible as tasks require. We extend "readout carriers" from one name token to a token set to better capture and express concept information and support counterfactual experiments. (ii) Concepts in downstream computation. Counterfactual experiments show that accessed concept information participates in downstream computation and reasoning. (iii) Development of cross-modal alignment and selective access. We develop two J-space metrics tracking the development of cross-modal concept alignment more clearly than hidden state cosine in controlled VLM training. The experiment also shows that reliable selective access develops later than concept accessibility. (iv) Shared functions across models. Across VLM families and sizes, we find shared patterns of concept accessibility, query-dependent selectivity and cross-task intervention effects despite differences in internal organisation. These findings offer an experimental basis to study GWT in multimodal artificial systems and how it can guide cross-modal alignment improvements.
papers.Core_Innovation: MC-Lens constructs a multimodal Jacobian lens mapping vision encoder and language decoder intermediate states to the decoder's output vocabulary, enabling direct comparison of concept accessibility across modalities and extending readout carriers from single tokens to token sets.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Multimodal Research, Semantic Search
papers.Decision_Perspective: AI labs must allocate funding to integrate MC-Lens into VLM interpretability pipelines within 6 months to enable selective concept auditing. Rivals delaying adoption will face transparency deficits in regulated deployments.
papers.Tags: Multimodal Concept Lens, Jacobian Lens, Selective Access, Vision-Language Models
papers.Hook: MC-Lens enables selective concept accessibility profiling in VLMs via multimodal Jacobian lensing.

papers.Title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
papers.Abstract: A passing UVM regression shows the design agrees with the reference model on what the scoreboard checks, not that it meets the specification. Bugs that pass every test yet violate the specification, termed scoreboard escapes, survive mature testbenches. We present Verify the Verifier, to our knowledge the first framework whose LLM-based Anomaly Cross-Checker examines a passing regression's traces against the specification. Of 564 bugs inserted into four OpenTitan IPs, 68 are candidate scoreboard escapes: non-equivalent, exercised by the tests, yet passing. The framework confirmed 41 as scoreboard escapes with assertions failing on the buggy design and proven on the original.
papers.Core_Innovation: The framework introduces an LLM-driven anomaly cross-checker that maps UVM regression execution traces to formal specification constraints, isolating scoreboard escapes where designs pass tests but violate specs.
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate R&D budget to integrate LLM cross-checking into existing UVM flows within 180 days. Discontinue scoreboard implementations that lack formal specification grounding.
papers.Tags: LLM, UVM, Specification, Scoreboard
papers.Hook: LLM cross-checks UVM regression traces against specification to expose scoreboard-escaping bugs.

papers.Title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
papers.Abstract: Graphic designs are ordered compositions of RGBA layers whose separation enables selection, movement, and reuse. Existing layered models represent each layer with a full-canvas or region-sized spatial latent grid, so representation size grows with the cumulative spatial extent of the layers. We present ProtoDiffusion, a latent-diffusion framework built on ProtoVAE, a multi-layer variational autoencoder that encodes a design into one shared spatial prototype and one candidate vector per layer. Each candidate conditions a shared decoder to reconstruct its corresponding RGBA layer. For $N$ layers, the representation contains $HW+N$ tokens before backbone-specific packing, compared with $NHW$ for full-grid-per-layer representations. ProtoDiffusion jointly denoises the prototype and a fixed set of candidate slots, conditioned on an image or text, with bounding boxes as optional layout guidance. The model leaves unneeded slots empty and determines the number of layers and, in absence of boxes, their layout, requiring neither as input. The same architecture supports both image-to-design and text-to-design. ProtoVAE achieves high-fidelity reconstruction from its compact shared latent representation, reaching 40.43 dB PSNR on layer crops. On the LayerD evaluation split, image-to-design achieves RGB L1 scores of 0.040 with bounding boxes and 0.057 without, with box-guided alpha soft IoU (0.850) comparable to the strongest fine-tuned baseline (0.871). On merged images, text-to-design reaches 66.41 FID versus 86.84 for FLUX.2 [klein], achieves a 0.860 text-accuracy score, and runs $19.1\times$ faster than the same-backbone generation-then-decomposition cascade.
papers.Core_Innovation: ProtoVAE replaces per-layer full-canvas latent grids with one shared prototype and N learnable candidate slots that condition a shared decoder, enabling dynamic layer count and token efficiency
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate prototyping budget to integrate ProtoDiffusion into existing generative pipelines within 12 months to validate token savings. Teams dependent on full-grid layer representations should assess migration feasibility within 6 months.
papers.Tags: token-efficient, generative layers, VAE, design automation
papers.Hook: Enables fixed-token layered generation with dynamic layer counting and box-guided layout.

papers.Title: Represented but misread: Post-training changes how language models read out what they represent
papers.Abstract: Does post-training change what a language model represents, or how this representation is read out into an answer? We compared linear probes with the models' own answers, analyzed with signal detection theory, in six open-weight base models and their post-trained versions. For judgments of whether German texts were written by a human or an AI, probes and word n-gram classifiers separated the classes well, but the answers did not and often ordered the texts inversely. Post-training lowered the sensitivity of the answers on average ($Δd' = -0.34$ across model families; -0.29 across three prompts). It also changed the use of a stated base rate: Base models shifted their log-odds by less than the stated change in prior odds, most post-trained models by more. In two models with stage-wise checkpoints, the change occurred during supervised fine-tuning, model stitching implicated the early layers, and from mid-depth on internal states at positions after the text, not those of the text, transferred the change between checkpoints. Our corpora cannot be shared, so we add a case reproducible from public data, the truth of negated statements. Here, post-training acted in the opposite direction: Probes decoded truth at or near ceiling in every model, the answers of several base models did not use it, and post-training repaired them; by mid-depth the repair resided at the positions after the statement; below it, the representation of the statement contributed, strongly in one of four models. In a training study, adding 2,000 correctly labeled authorship judgments of news texts to otherwise identical fine-tuning data improved the answers on our newspaper and textbook corpora and inverted them on the chats, where they followed a news-trained probe of the base model. Post-training thus changed how a judgment is read out of what a model represents, and a small training signal can set its direction.
papers.Core_Innovation: Post-training degrades answer sensitivity (Δd' = -0.34) by shifting readout mechanisms rather than representations, with early-layer internal states after text positions implicated via model stitching.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: AI Safety, Synthetic Data, Digital Forensics
papers.Decision_Perspective: Mandate read-out sensitivity audits for all post-trained LLMs before deployment. Trigger these audits within 30 days of any fine-tuning completion.
papers.Tags: Post-training, Readout, Signal Detection, Early Layers, Base Rate
papers.Hook: Post-training reconfigures read-out mechanisms, degrading answer sensitivity despite preserved representations

papers.Title: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs
papers.Abstract: Multimodal image generation systems have made rapid progress and increasingly emphasize content safety. However, their safety mechanisms tend to rely on a single modality and lack joint consideration of both visual content and text prompts, particularly in instruction-guided image editing, where the uploaded image may itself carry risk. We thus introduce EditSafetyBench, a benchmark that measures system-level safety awareness of advanced image editing systems, containing 5,940 image-instruction pairs, covering safe and unsafe images across 11 risk categories and three edit intents. We then probe the benchmark dataset on four systems, including Gemini, GPT, Qwen API, and Qwen Local. Based on our evaluation, we observe a systematic text-vision safety mismatch: Gemini and GPT refuse 87.1\% and 81.6\% cases containing unsafe-intent editing prompts, while only refusing 24.2\% and 22.4\% cases with both unsafe images and neutral instructions. At the category level, most risks are considered inconsistently by different systems, e.g., GPT allows 70.4\% editing attempts of unsafe political content while Gemini only allows 34.8\%. Notably, sexual content shows the strongest visual sensitivity, likely benefiting from mature NSFW identification works. Our findings highlight the need for safety guardrails that jointly reason over both visual and textual modalities in image editing systems.
papers.Core_Innovation: EditSafetyBench constructs the first joint image-text safety annotation schema across 11 risk categories and 3 edit intents, permitting systematic measurement of modality-specific refusal patterns
papers.Decision_Perspective: Require multimodal safety audits for all generative image editing APIs within 120 days. Integrate EditSafetyBench into vendor certification pipelines by Q3 2026.
papers.Tags: multimodal safety, image editing, vision-text alignment, benchmark
papers.Hook: New benchmark quantifies text-vision safety mismatches in multimodal image editing.

papers.Title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild
papers.Abstract: Generative engines synthesize retrieved web pages into answers, recommendations, and rankings. Generative engine optimization (GEO) services sell visibility in these answers by publishing promotional articles on user-generated-content (UGC) platforms for paying clients. Such promotion raises concerns in medical and financial domains, where misleading advice can cause harm. To study the severity of this problem, we measure one such paid-content operation across three major Chinese UGC platforms, uncovering 1,985 accounts associated with the network comprising 466,357 inferred promotional placements. We find that the network promotes products across diverse categories through a growing pool of accounts, conducting coordinated campaigns spanning months across multiple platforms while evolving its listicle content over time. Across nine generative engines from both the US and China, we find that 4.5% to 20% of retrievable cited pages are attributable to the network, depending on how strictly attribution is drawn. On eight of these engines, its clients are named in 52% of answers, against 68% for category leaders. Our work demonstrates the effectiveness of UGC GEO placement at influencing generative engine outcomes, and reveals content-level defenses as insufficient against coordinated UGC placements, where account-level and platform-level signals are necessary for proper defense.
papers.Core_Innovation: Developed a mapping methodology to link disparate UGC accounts to a single promotional network across multiple platforms. It empirically measures the citation capture rate of GEO operations across nine different LLM-based engines.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Cybersecurity, AI Safety, Trust And Safety Software
papers.Disrupted_Sectors: Digital Marketing, SEO Agencies, UGC Platforms
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate funding for GEO detection system development within enterprise search platforms over the next 18 months to disrupt covert promotional infiltration. Mandate quarterly compliance audits for medical and financial UGC content starting Q2 2026.
papers.Tags: Generative Engine Optimization, GEO, LLM Manipulation, UGC, Information Integrity
papers.Hook: GEOHunter maps covert GEO networks across generative engines with real-time placement tracking

papers.Title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
papers.Abstract: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value? We argue this is a question about a single cognitive trait, metacognitive calibration: the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their judgments. We develop a trait theory of reviewer value to make it precise. The theory makes five claims: value is governed by calibration rather than by activity, speed, agreement, or tenure; calibration leaves observable traces in behavioral telemetry; those traces are non-diagnostic on their own, because the fast, low-revision signature of a calibrated expert is indistinguishable from that of a confident novice until it is gated by outcomes; human calibration and a model's self-knowledge are the same construct, so the joint system should defer to whichever agent is better calibrated on each item; and individual calibration is causally identifiable only above the level of the single judgment. We ground each claim in a six-month production window of an AI-assisted accounting system (541621 reviewer events, 483 reviewers), and find that a purely behavioral expertise profile inverts the ground truth, scoring an overconfident cohort (5.2 percent correction survival) higher than genuine experts (99.2 percent); that reviewer quality is flat across tenure, so the trait is not learned on the job; and that the same calibration logic that separates good from bad reviewers, applied to the model, concentrates 92.5 percent of human effort on genuine errors. We close with the boundary the theory must respect: under majority-vote aggregation, individual causal value is unidentifiable.
papers.Core_Innovation: Positions metacognitive calibration as the exclusive determinant of reviewer value, enabling item-level deferral to the better-calibrated agent regardless of expertise or tenure. Demonstrates that calibration traces in behavioral telemetry are non-diagnostic until gated by outcome correctness.
papers.Decision_Perspective: Invest in real-time metacognitive calibration tracking for human-AI decision pipelines within 18 months. Retire legacy expert-review systems that prioritize tenure over calibrated confidence.
papers.Tags: metacognitive calibration, human-AI cooperation, reviewer value, trait theory, behavioral telemetry
papers.Hook: Calibration, not expertise, determines human-AI value per decision.

papers.Title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
papers.Abstract: AI systems are built across many organizations that contribute models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets. While the layers of the AI stack are relatively well understood, the relationships between actors and components across layers remains sparsely documented. In this work, we focus on the organizations that make up the AI supply chain: the complex network of actors that contribute to the development and deployment of AI. We motivate the examination of the organizational AI supply chain---highlighting concerns about concentration, power, chokepoints, cascading failures, fragmented accountability, and risk---then describe our pipeline for mapping the AI supply chain. Our pipeline yields our main contribution: a multilayered, large-scale dataset of actors and relationships in the AI ecosystem, annotated with dates, descriptions, types, tags, and more. This work takes a step toward systematically mapping and measuring the AI supply chain and its properties, cataloging how models, data, chips, infrastructure, capital, and even talent flow between organizations. This data enable critical examinations of industry relationships and yield insights into the political economy of AI development and concentration. We provide several illustrative analyses, including studying the most central actors, analyzing network concentration, and identifying communities and chokepoints. While our dataset is fairly comprehensive, it is also necessarily incomplete: public documents omit private deals, and coverage is shaped by search design. Together, the approach, data, and findings aim to serve as a resource for studying the AI ecosystem. The dataset is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/sarahcen/ai-supply-chain and can be explored interactively at https://aisupplychains.org/.
papers.Core_Innovation: Introduces a pipeline that constructs and annotates a multilayer AI actor-network dataset with dates, types, and tags.
papers.Decision_Perspective: Mandate AI supply-chain audits for all portfolio companies within 6 months to expose hidden dependencies. Discontinue investments in AI startups lacking transparent model and compute sourcing.
papers.Tags: AI Supply Chain, Market Concentration, Actor Networks
papers.Hook: Enables systematic mapping of AI actor networks and market concentration.

papers.Title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
papers.Abstract: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation. However, existing harness evolution methods often overlook implicit requirements and interaction needs, while using a single evolution agent to modify the harness and benchmark scores to select changes. This process often produces narrow patches and leads to benchmark-specific local optima. We introduce Agentic Harness Engineering Beta (AHE-Beta), a requirement-centered loop that brings real-world engineering practices into harness evolution. The loop consists of three steps: (1) User-driven evaluation lets simulated users raise their requirements as issues while they work with the harness over multiple turns. (2) Team-based modification implements those requirements as generalizable changes rather than task-specific patches. (3) Requirement-driven selection merges a change only when it resolves a verified requirement and passes review. Empirically, on held-out tasks, AHE-Beta raises pass@1 from 21.9% to 33.3% while using 40.8% fewer tokens than Base Harness, and achieves higher pass@1 than Claude Code, Meta-Harness, and AHE. In a blind human A/B test, real users prefer AHE-Beta in 31 of 48 valid pairs and rate it higher on all five dimensions, matching the directional preference of the user simulator. The human A/B results show that AHE-Beta achieves its goal of aligning harness evolution with real-world user requirements. Without further evolution, the gains transfer to GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with pass@1 improvements of 15.8% and 5.3% over Base Harness. Together, these results show that requirement-centered harness evolution is a more general method for improving agent capabilities.
papers.Core_Innovation: A three-loop requirement-centered evolution uses simulated users to emit requirement issues over multiple turns, a team-based modifier generates generalizable changes, and review-gated selection merges only changes resolving verified requirements
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate engineering resources to prototype AHE-Beta's requirement-centered loop in our agent harness workflow within the next quarter. Track benchmark convergence and requirement resolution metrics to evaluate replacement of single-agent evolution methods.
papers.Tags: Agent Harnesses, Requirement Engineering, Multi-turn Simulation
papers.Hook: Multi-turn user simulation drives generalizable harness evolution beyond benchmark-local optima

papers.Title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation
papers.Abstract: We study two-layer neural networks trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a multi-index teacher model, focusing on how first-layer parameters orthogonal to the teacher subspace affect generalization. We decompose the first-layer weights into a signal component aligned with the teacher and an orthogonal complement, and analyze their joint SGD dynamics together with the second layer in the proportional limit. We show that although SGD updates to the complement are initially isotropic, the training dynamics induce teacher-dependent spectral spikes in the complement Gram matrix. This emergent anisotropy provides a concrete mechanism by which representation variance is amplified, and generalization degrades. To isolate this effect, we introduce Decomposed Dynamics, an analytically tractable surrogate whose asymptotic test-error dynamics coincide with those of SGD. In simulations with a ReLU student, freezing the directions of the orthogonal complement improves generalization relative to training them. Finally, we show that the signal component rapidly aligns with the second-layer weights, revealing strong cross-layer coupling even in this shallow setting. Together, our results provide a dynamical explanation for how feature learning outside the teacher subspace harms generalization.
papers.Core_Innovation: The paper proposes Decomposed Dynamics, a surrogate model whose asymptotic test-error trajectory coincides with full SGD, and proves that teacher-induced spectral spikes in the orthogonal complement Gram matrix are the primary cause of representation variance inflation and degradation.
papers.Benefiting_Sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Neural Network Training
papers.Decision_Perspective: Allocate funding to integrate Decomposed Dynamics surrogates into SGD pipelines within 6 months. Halt SGD training runs for ReLU models that do not account for orthogonal complement spectral spikes at scale.
papers.Tags: SGD dynamics, generalization, spectral spikes, orthogonal complement
papers.Hook: Identify teacher-induced spectral spikes to control variance in SGD training

papers.Title: Equivariant Modeling with Polynomial Features via Minimal Homogeneous Generators
papers.Abstract: We present a general framework for modeling and learning equivariant functions between finite dimensional semisimple real group representations, unifying constructions developed across many application areas. Our model is a linear combination of equivariant polynomial features whose coefficients are arbitrary learnable functions of invariant polynomial features. We take as features minimal homogeneous generators for the invariant algebra and the covariant module over the invariant algebra, up to prescribed degrees. We provide a Python package that automatically computes these features and fits the resulting models to training data. The algorithm for feature computation requires explicit isotypic decompositions of the input and output representations, along with explicit Clebsch-Gordan decompositions of the tensor product of irreducible representations, and achieves speedups over alternative methods in computational algebra.
